title: The Power of Stance
text:
Many readers assume that a writer who uses words like 'clearly' or 'undoubtedly' is presenting a neutral fact. In reality, such words signal stance. They tell the reader how confident the writer feels about a claim, and they can subtly persuade the reader to accept it without question.

Consider the difference between 'The policy failed' and 'The policy seems to have failed.' The first sentence states a judgment as fact, while the second softens it with a hedge. Skilled writers choose between these forms deliberately, depending on how much evidence they have and how much they want to appear open to debate.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do words like 'clearly' and 'undoubtedly' show?
options: The date the article was published

questions.text: What does the second paragraph say the first sentence does?
What can be inferred about a writer who uses a hedge such as 'seems to'?
options: They want to avoid all debate
They are probably less certain or open to other views
They are unaware of how readers react

questions.text: Why might a writer deliberately choose a word that signals stance?
options: To make a claim seem more neutral
To influence how the reader perceives a claim

vocabulary.definition: the writer's attitude or position toward a claim
a word or phrase that softens a statement
to make someone believe or agree with something

paragraph_translations: Muchos lectores suponen que un escritor que usa palabras como 'clearly' o 'undoubtedly' presenta un hecho neutral. En realidad, esas palabras señalan una postura. Indican al lector cuánta seguridad tiene el escritor sobre una afirmación, y pueden persuadir sutilmente al lector para que la acepte sin cuestionarla.

Considere la diferencia entre 'The policy failed' y 'The policy seems to have failed'. La primera oración presenta un juicio como si fuera un hecho, mientras que la segunda lo suaviza con un modalizador. Los escritores hábiles eligen entre estas formas de manera deliberada, según la cantidad de evidencia que tienen y cuánto quieren parecer abiertos al debate.
